title: Subspace Selection based Prompt Tuning with Nonconvex Nonsmooth Black-Box Optimization

problem.claim: Black-box prompt tuning must operate in settings where users have API access to language models but no direct access to their internal structures or gradients.

gap.claim: Previous black-box prompt-tuning methods require many API calls because they choose the optimization subspace randomly.

contributions.claim: A black-box prompt-tuning framework combines subspace learning and selection with derivative-free optimization.
The framework uses the Zeroth-Order Mini-Batch Stochastic Proximal Gradient method to address nonconvex optimization with nonsmooth nonconvex regularizers.
Nonsmooth nonconvex regularizers, including the indicator function of the l0 constraint, are used to select subspaces for prompt optimization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present their framework as novel and identify the incorporation of nonsmooth nonconvex regularizers for subspace selection as a key innovation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On a few labeled samples, the proposed black-box prompt-tuning method reportedly achieves similar performance to methods applicable to LMaaS while using much fewer API calls.

narrative_sequence.summary: The method targets API-only language-model access without internal structures or gradients.
The framework explores a low-dimensional subspace of continuous prompts.
Prior black-box prompt tuning uses randomly selected subspaces and therefore needs substantial API calls.
The proposed approach uses ZO-MB-SPG and nonsmooth nonconvex regularizers, including an l0 constraint indicator, to select prompt-optimization subspaces.
The authors report similar performance with substantially fewer API calls on a few labeled samples.

unknowns: Task datasets, model identities, baseline methods, and exact API-call counts are not specified.
Optimization guarantees, hyperparameters, and implementation details are not provided.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or generalization beyond the reported experiments.
